item.title: Configuring Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) with Spring Security: Multiple Solutions
item.description:
“Configuring Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) with Spring Security: Multiple Solutions”

When deploying web applications, especially those involving separate frontend and backend services, encountering Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) restrictions is frequent. Browsers enforce these policies for security, which is why tools like curl might work while browser-initiated AJAX requests fail. If you are using Spring Security, you must explicitly configure CORS support to prevent Spring Security from blocking these requests before they reach Spring MVC handlers.

item.title: Spring Security CORS Issues: Preflight OPTIONS Requests and Configuration
item.description:
“Spring Security CORS Issues: Preflight OPTIONS Requests and Configuration”

When building modern web applications, especially those involving frontend frameworks like Angular or React communicating with a Spring Boot backend, you often encounter Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) challenges. A common stumbling block is the handling of preflight requests, which use the HTTP OPTIONS method. These requests are sent by browsers before the actual request (like GET, POST, etc.) to determine if the server permits the cross-origin request. If not configured correctly, these preflight requests can fail, leading to various errors in your browser’s developer console.
